## Immutable State Patterns

- Represent application state as immutable data classes — **NEVER** mutate state objects in place.
- Use `sealed` classes (Dart) or discriminated unions (TypeScript) for state variants — exhaustive `switch` expressions **MUST** cover every variant at compile time.
- Generate immutable models with `copyWith` methods — use code generation (`freezed`, `built_value`) to eliminate hand-written boilerplate.
- State transitions **MUST** produce new instances — **NEVER** modify fields on existing state objects.
- Use value equality (not reference equality) for state comparison — this enables efficient change detection and prevents unnecessary UI rebuilds.
- Keep state classes flat — **NEVER** nest mutable collections inside immutable wrappers.
- Separate UI state (loading, error, success) from domain entities — do not overload domain models with presentation concerns.
